summary: Base moves $50 -> $45: three sites of the 30 AMP + Water type (19, 20, 21) take 30-35 ft, so the type counts. $50 and $55 confirmed, June 2027 and November 2026. Weekend 2-night and holiday 3-night minimums added. Pond stands on about 4 RV sites; most RV pads are not on the pond.
flags: GATE: posted $45 (sites 19-21, 30-35 ft) / $50 (30/50 and full hookup) / $55 (50 amp), plus $8 reservation fee once per stay and Campspot 3%. Passes the $50 gate. Earlier read had this at $50-55 at the line because the whole $45 type was left out for its 20-ft sites 14-18; 3 of its 8 fit. Not a Good Sam Park (stored). No gateway within 40 km (Indianapolis 92 km). Family has not stayed.

GOOGLE: 4.5 from 316 reviews, phone (765) 592-6458 matches the operator's page. All five newest reviews read are warm ('It's very clean and staff are friendly', 'Showers are nice and always clean', 'a much quieter' base for Turkey Run, dated 2/23/2026). No complaint in those five; I read no further.

BORDERLINE? No, on price and reviews. Policies worth knowing, operator's page: 'No Refunds will be given for canceled reservations or unused nights'; 'Deposits are not refundable'; 'One Vehicles per site'; pet fee per pet per stay.

SEASONAL READ: not mostly seasonal on what I can see. Engine sells 40 RV sites nightly. Its map also draws about 28 pads in the west strip that sell under no bookable type; the operator doesn't say what they are, possibly seasonal. No seasonal rate read, no resident language in the five reviews.

WATER: 'pond' rests on a minority of pads. On the operator's Campspot map only about 3-4 RV pads, on the pond's east shore, sit by the 4-acre pond; the RV strip along US-41 is well west of it, ~100+ m on my read of the map. Satellite shows gravel pads on that east shore; I did not measure pad-to-water to the metre. Waterfront left as stored.
PIN: 39.8165,-87.2364 is at the US-41 entrance, ~100-150 m from the RV strip; fine.
DRY LOT: a $27 'Dry Lot' type (2 sites) has no description or rig list on Campspot; not used as base. Ask if a cheaper base matters.
